text.text: The repeated high-rise blocks create a uniform environment with little architectural variety or local identity.
Large open areas between buildings are mostly inactive, creating empty spaces with limited social or recreational use.
Residential areas are often separated from shops and basic services, increasing travel distances for everyday needs.
Wide roads and vehicle-focused planning create barriers between neighbourhoods and make walking and cycling less convenient.
Open spaces around the housing blocks provide few safe or engaging areas for children to play and interact.
The lack of active public spaces and shared facilities limits opportunities for residents to meet and build a stronger community.
